scamCategories.title: Types of Scams We Detect
scamCategories.subtitle: Comprehensive fraud detection covering all major scam types in India  from UPI fraud to phishing links and digital arrest scams.

categories.title: UPI Fraud Detection
categories.description: Fake UPI collect requests and bank impersonation trick Indians into approving fraudulent payments. Common patterns include 'cashback refund' collect requests, fake payment screenshots, and QR code scams. RakshaAI checks UPI IDs against reported fraud databases so you know before you send.

categories.title: Digital Arrest Scams
categories.description: Fraudsters impersonate CBI, Narcotics Control Bureau, ED, or Supreme Court officials over video calls to 'digitally arrest' victims and extort 'bail fees'. These highly orchestrated scams have extracted thousands of crore from professionals, retirees, and students across India. Never engage  hang up and call the real agency's published number.

categories.title: Fake E-commerce Websites
categories.description: Cloned shopping sites offer iPhones, electronics, and clothing at 60–80% discounts to harvest card details and advance payments. These sites mimic Flipkart, Amazon, and Myntra layouts and disappear after collecting orders. Always verify any unfamiliar shopping URL on RakshaAI before entering payment details.

categories.title: Investment & Trading Scams
categories.description: WhatsApp groups fronting SEBI analysts, fake stock trading apps promising guaranteed returns, and pig-butchering crypto platforms are among India's fastest-growing fraud types. Victims typically lose ₹10–50 lakh. Verify any investment platform at SEBI's official portal before depositing a single rupee.

categories.title: Task-Based Job Scams
categories.description: Part-time job offers on WhatsApp promise ₹5,000–₹15,000 daily for liking YouTube videos or completing simple tasks. After victims earn small test payouts, they are pressured into depositing ₹10,000–₹2,00,000 for 'premium tasks' and never see the money again. These scams spread via Telegram and Instagram as well.

categories.title: Phishing & Fake Links
categories.description: Malicious links delivered via SMS, email, and WhatsApp impersonate IRCTC, banks, NHAI, and government portals to steal login credentials or install APK malware. A single click can give attackers access to your bank account. Paste any suspicious link into RakshaAI's website checker before opening it.

categories.title: Romance & Dating Scams
categories.description: Fraudsters spend weeks or months building emotional relationships on Facebook, Instagram, and matrimonial apps before requesting money for medical emergencies, visa fees, or investment opportunities. India reported a 68% rise in romance fraud cases in 2024. Always independently verify someone's identity before transferring any money.

categories.title: Fake Loan Apps
categories.description: Unlicensed loan apps charge 200–500% effective annual interest, harvest your entire phone contact list on install, and blackmail defaulters by sending doctored images to family and colleagues. Verify any loan app against the RBI's registered NBFC list at rbi.org.in before applying.

categories.title: Phone & SMS Scams
categories.description: Calls impersonating TRAI, banks, UIDAI, courier companies, and government departments account for millions of fraud attempts daily. Common scripts include 'your SIM will be disconnected', 'a parcel with narcotics in your name', and 'your Aadhaar is linked to a crime'. Always hang up and verify through official channels  never act on an incoming call.

categories.title: Cryptocurrency Scams
categories.description: Fake crypto exchanges, Ponzi schemes disguised as DeFi staking platforms, and task-based 'crypto mining' apps promise 5–15% daily returns. Most are controlled from overseas and funds are unrecoverable once transferred. Report any suspicious crypto platform or wallet address to RakshaAI to protect other Indians.

safetyTips.title: How to Stay Safe from Online Scams
safetyTips.subtitle: Practical habits that reduce common online scam risks

tips.title: Never Share OTP
tips.description: Your OTP is a one-time password that authenticates only you. No legitimate bank, UPI app, UIDAI, or government department will ever call or message you asking for it. If someone asks for your OTP, it is always a scam  hang up immediately.

tips.title: Don't Rush Decisions
tips.description: Scammers deliberately create panic and urgency  'your account will be blocked in 10 minutes', 'act now or face arrest'. Legitimate banks and government agencies never rush you into instant decisions. Take a breath, end the call, and verify independently.

tips.title: Check Before Clicking
tips.description: Before clicking any link received via SMS, WhatsApp, or email, paste it into RakshaAI's free website checker at rakshaai.co. Phishing links often use subtle typos like 'amaz0n.in' or 'sbi-secure.net'. A 5-second check can save your savings.

tips.title: Verify Caller Identity
tips.description: If you get an unexpected call from your 'bank', 'police', or 'government agency', hang up and call back on the official number published on their website or the back of your card. Never use a number given by the caller  it could be a forwarded scam line.

tips.title: Money Only Goes Out (UPI rule)
tips.description: UPI collect requests always send money out of your account  you never receive money by approving one. Scammers send fake 'refund' or 'cashback' collect requests. Approve a collect request only when you are consciously paying someone you fully trust.

tips.title: Use Official Apps Only
tips.description: Download banking, UPI, and investment apps only from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store, and only from the official publisher listed by your bank. Fake apps harvested over 10 crore data records from Indian users in 2024 alone.

tips.title: Protect Family Members
tips.description: Elderly relatives and teenagers are the most targeted demographics for scam calls and fake job offers. Share the 1930 cybercrime helpline number with your family and teach them one rule: never share OTPs, PINs, or Aadhaar details over phone or WhatsApp.

tips.title: Report Suspicious Activity
tips.description: Reporting scams at RakshaAI, on 1930, or at cybercrime.gov.in protects thousands of other Indians who might encounter the same phone number, UPI ID, or website. Every report strengthens the shared intelligence network and makes future fraud harder to execute.

questions.question: What is RakshaAI and how does it work?
questions.answer: RakshaAI provides free consumer checks for supported websites, UPI IDs, phone numbers and documents. It evaluates available risk signals and returns a Trust Score with context to support your decision. A secure user account is required, and no automated result is a guarantee of legitimacy.

questions.question: Is it really completely free? No hidden charges?
questions.answer: Individuals can currently run supported checks without a paid subscription. Business verification and future enterprise products may be paid separately.

questions.question: Who is this service for?
questions.answer: For everyone! Students doing online shopping, parents worried about their children's safety, senior citizens wanting to verify bank links, small business owners protecting their data - every Indian. You don't need any technical knowledge, just paste a link and get results.

questions.question: What is a Trust Score and how do I understand it?
questions.answer: Trust Score is a 0-100 rating. Above 70 = Generally Safe, 40-70 = Somewhat Suspicious (be careful), Below 40 = High Risk (avoid it). We don't just give you a number - we tell you WHY it got that score. Like 'domain is very new' or 'SSL certificate is invalid' - in simple language.

questions.question: How accurate is the Trust Score?
questions.answer: Very accurate for detecting known threats, but no system is 100% perfect. We check multiple databases and use advanced AI, but always use common sense too. If something feels wrong, trust your instincts even if our score says it's okay.

questions.question: What are the most common types of scams in India?
questions.answer: Fake shopping websites, phishing WhatsApp messages, fraudulent payment links, lottery scams, fake job offers, romance scams on dating apps, and investment fraud. Always verify before clicking or paying anything.

questions.question: What are your top tips to stay safe online?
questions.answer: 1) Always check suspicious links here first 2) Never share OTPs or passwords 3) Be skeptical of 'too good to be true' offers 4) Verify bank messages by calling your bank directly 5) Don't download apps from unknown sources 6) Use strong, unique passwords.

questions.question: What data do you collect about me?
questions.answer: We keep minimal data. Check queries are anonymised and not associated with your identity. We collect only what is necessary to operate the service and improve our detection models. We do not sell data or share it with advertisers. See our Privacy Policy for full details.

questions.question: What if a safe website shows as risky?
questions.answer: It can happen! If you think we made a mistake, please contact us with the link and we'll review it manually. Sometimes legitimate new websites get flagged because they're very new or have some technical issues.

questions.question: How do I report a scam or fraudulent website?
questions.answer: Use the 'Report a Scam' button on our website, or email us directly. The more details you provide, the better we can help protect others. Include the URL, what happened, and any screenshots if possible.
